# Switchboard (dsh-switchboard)
English | 中文
Command DeepSeek Harness Agents from your phone through Telegram and Feishu (Lark) bots: send the Ag
ent text, photos, files, and voice notes, watch replies arrive as they are written, answer tool appr
ovals and the Agent's questions, follow long tasks for completion notices, and browse every chat in
the Web UI, where any Session can be linked to a chat.
The bots are other clients of the Web host. They create and prompt Sessions through `ctx.sessionCont
roller`, the same path the Web UI uses, so chat Sessions appear in the Web sidebar and Web Sessions
can be taken over or followed. Sessions a bot creates go into the Web Workspace for their working di
rectory (created on first use).
## Lines
A **line** is one bot on one chat platform plus the people allowed to use it. Configure as many as y
ou need, for example Telegram for yourself and Feishu for your team; each line has its own credentia
ls, allowed users and chats, and default working directory. One Session can be linked to chats on se
veral lines at once, and replies, approvals, and questions go to each of them. Chats are keyed `line
:chat id` (for example `feishu:oc_xxx`); the original Telegram line (`telegram`) keeps bare ids, so
bindings and history from earlier releases carry over. Supported: **Telegram** and **Feishu / Lark**
indings and history from earlier releases carry over. Supported: **Telegram** and **Feishu / Lark**.
## Quick start
1. Install into a Web profile: **Plugins → Add plugin** with `dsh-switchboard`, or `dsh plugin --pro

file web add dsh-switchboard`.
2. Open **Plugins → Installed → Switchboard** (or **Plugin settings**
in the sidebar panel), add a line under **Lines**, fill in its credentials and **Allowed users** (s
end `/whoami` to the bot for your id), set the **Default working directory**, and **Save**. Changes
he bot for your id), set the **Default working directory**, and **Save**. Changes apply immediately.
**Telegram line**: create a bot with @BotFather (`/newbot`), then **+ Telegram line** and paste the
token. Allowed users are Telegram ids or `@usernames`.
**Feishu line**: Feishu delivers events over the Open Platform's persistent connection, so no public
: Feishu delivers events over the Open Platform's persistent connection, so no public URL is needed.
**By QR (recommended)**: **+ Feishu line** → **Create a Feishu app by QR**, scan with the Feishu app
(or **Open in browser** on this computer), and confirm. The bot, permissions, the `im.message.recei
ve_v1` event, and the `card.action.trigger` callback are filled in; the Host stores the App Secret i
n the credentials store (it never reaches the browser), the scanner is added to the allowed users, a
nd the line is saved and connects. For an existing app, **Complete permissions** adds what is missin
saved and connects. For an existing app, **Complete permissions** adds what is missing the same way.

**By hand**:
1. On the Feishu Open Platform (or Lark) create a self-built app and add the **Bot** ca

pability.
2. Grant `im:message.p2p_msg:readonly`, `im:message.group_at_msg:readonly`, `im:message:se
nd_as_bot`, and `im:resource`; optionally `contact:user.base:readonly` (names) and `im:chat:readonly

` (group names).
3. Add **+ Feishu line** with the **App ID** (`cli_…`) and **App Secret** and save:

Feishu lets you pick the persistent connection only while a client is connected.
4. Under **Events
and callbacks**, choose **Receive events through persistent connection** and add the event `im.messa

ge.receive_v1`; do the same for callbacks and add `card.action.trigger` (buttons need it).
5. Publis
h a version, message the bot `/whoami`, and add the open_id it replies with (`ou_…`, per app; user_i
d and union_id also match) to the line's allowed users.

## In the chat
| Command | Effect |
| text, photo, file, voice | Goes to the current Session; one is started in the default directory if

needed |
| `/menu` | Buttons for common actions (new session, sessions, model, mode, stop, compact,

status, help); the easiest way in Feishu |
| `/new [dir]` | New Session; without a directory, pick

the default or a recent one |
| `/cwd <dir>` | Working directory for this chat's new Sessions |
| `/

sessions` | Recent Sessions with titles, as buttons that switch |
| `/use <n\|sessionId>` | Switch t

o an existing Session (Web ones too) |
| `/watch [n\|sessionId]` | Follow a Session's completions an

d approvals; no argument lists them |
| `/unwatch <n\|sessionId\|all>` | Stop following |
| `/stop`

| Stop current work |
| `/steer <text>` | Steer the running turn |
| `/queue`, `/cancel <n\|all>` |

Show or drop queued messages |
| `/model [name]` | Show or switch the Session's model (buttons, fuzz

y match; the Web default is untouched) |
| `/mode [mode]` | Show or switch the Session's permission

mode |
| `/get <path>` | Fetch a file or list a directory inside the working directory (symlinks can

not escape it) |
| `/fork` | Branch from the latest finished turn into a new Session; the original s

tays |
| `/status` | Session, model, directory, run state, line, context use, this turn's time, goal

, todos, subagents, and queue |
| Reply to a notice or reply | Goes to the Session that message belo

ngs to, without `/use`; the chat's own Session stays, and that turn's replies come back here |
| `/d
igest` | Roundup of followed Sessions over 24 hours: finished, failed, waiting for you, and running.
Set **Daily digest of followed Sessions** to get it once a day instead of a notice per turn; failur

es, approvals, and questions still arrive at once |
| `/board`, `/board off` | Live board: one messa

ge that keeps showing every Session's state, with buttons to switch; close it |
| `/away [duration\|
off]` | Away mode: approvals and questions wait for you instead of going to the Web UI, with a repor

t when you are back. Durations like `30m`, `2h`, `1d` |
| `/schedule`, `/schedule add …` | Manage sc

heduled tasks (admins); see below |

## Models
A `/model` choice for the Session > the plugin page's **Bot default model** for Sessions a bot creat
es > the Web default. Neither changes the Web default.
